basis: Judged against shots.json still_prompt and notes for L18, held against its chain parent L17, plus the era global_prompt_suffix.
ruling: PARK - the most serious failure in the batch. This is a delta that re-invented its parent instead of holding it, AND missed the one geometry its own prompt was rewritten (R-12) to pin. The style axis is fine in isolation (warm ink at 12.3deg, flat cel, chromatic at 0.2706); what fails is content, continuity and period.
why: The two phone slabs lie FLAT on the platform splayed open like a book instead of standing upright butted face to face and locked up, so the mirrored fight the line needs is not depicted; the held set was re-invented (plate-glass panels became a wooden proscenium, the red scuffed arc became faint scratches, the spotlight and platform lighting changed, the cases changed proportion); and the crowd is a different crowd in contemporary short-sleeved dress rather than L17's 1980s coats and headscarves, which is an era break as well as a continuity break.

dsg.q: Are two flat black glass slabs present at the front edge of the platform?
dsg.note: Two black glass slabs are present on the platform.

dsg.q: Do the slabs STAND UPRIGHT, butted face to face and shoved hard against each other, locked up like the two cases behind them?
dsg.note: FAIL, and it is the exact error R-12 was written to fix. The slabs LIE FLAT, splayed open like an opened book - not upright, not butted face to face, not locked up. Two phones lying face-up on a plinth read as display stock, so the mirrored fight that 'and Apple fight over the phone market' needs is simply not depicted. This is the shot's entire payload.

dsg.q: Is there a matching dent where they meet, with their bottom edges skidded apart under the push?
dsg.note: Short-circuited by the parent failure: with the slabs lying flat there is no upright contact geometry for a dent or a skid to describe.

dsg.q: Is the rest of the display held exactly as established in L17 - plate glass, black platform with its red scuffed arc, spotlight, case proportions?
dsg.note: FAIL. Essentially nothing carried: the plate-glass side panels became a wooden proscenium frame; the red scuffed arc became faint pink scratches; the spotlight cone changed shape and the platform gained a large cream light pool; the cases changed proportion and gained scuff marks they did not have. A delta frame's whole contract is that only the authored change moves.

dsg.q: Is the crowd of passers-by held - same people, in coats and headscarves with shopping bags?
dsg.note: FAIL, twice over. A wholly different set of people, drawn smaller with a different face treatment and repositioned from the flanks to a band across the top - a continuity break; AND they wear short-sleeved t-shirts, contemporary casual wear and modern hairstyles - an ERA break. The frame's costume no longer reads 1983.

dsg.q: Figure integrity: 2 arms / 2 legs, plausible hands, no fusions?
dsg.note: No amputations or fused limbs found. The crowd's anatomy is sound; its identity and period are the problem.

dsg.q: Era register: warm outline, flat cel, chromatic; and is red used semantically only?
dsg.note: Outline and cel are correct (ink hue 12.3deg, R-B +27.2; median saturation 0.2706) - but the red accent lost its semantics. In L17 red is the contact arc, the punch element; here it survives only as scattered scratch marks with no single semantic referent, which the era suffix licenses red for.

dsg.q: Lettering: is no unauthored text or brand mark drawn?
dsg.note: No lettering, no brand marks.
